title: Protocol to generate stable knockout lines in Strongyloides stercoralis
author: Banerjee, Walsh, et al.
materials: Platinum Taq DNA polymerase PCR kit

steps.title: Measure plasmid concentrations
steps.instruction: Determine the concentration of each plasmid stock (Cas9, sgRNA, HDR #1, HDR #2) using a Nanodrop or equivalent micro‑volume spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Prepare Microinjection Mix 1
steps.instruction: Dilute the Cas9 (50 ng/µL), sgRNA (80 ng/µL) and HDR #1 plasmid (80 ng/µL) in BU saline or ddH₂O to a final volume of 10–20 µL so that the final concentrations match Table 1. Spin the mixture through a 0.22 µm filter column at 16 200 × g for 1–2 min. Optionally re‑measure total DNA concentration; mixes within ±10–20 ng/µL of the expected value are acceptable.

steps.title: Prepare Microinjection Mix 2
steps.instruction: Dilute the Cas9 (50 ng/µL), sgRNA (80 ng/µL) and HDR #2 plasmid (80 ng/µL) in BU saline or ddH₂O to a final volume of 10–20 µL so that the final concentrations match Table 2. Spin the mixture through a 0.22 µm filter column at 16 200 × g for 1–2 min. Optionally re‑measure total DNA concentration; mixes within ±10–20 ng/µL of the expected value are acceptable.

steps.title: Store microinjection mixes
steps.instruction: Use the mixes on the same day or store at –20 °C. If using two sgRNA constructs targeting distinct sites, add each at a final concentration of 40 ng/µL.

steps.title: Make agarose injection pads
steps.instruction: Prepare a 5 % agarose solution in ddH₂O, boil until fully dissolved, and keep the tube in a 95 °C heat block. Using a glass Pasteur pipette, place ~180 µL of the hot agarose onto a 48 × 60 mm coverslip, immediately place a second coverslip on top, and remove the top coverslip after 5–10 s. Dry the pads for 16–24 h at 22–23 °C. Pads may be stored at 22–23 °C for up to 2 months but should not be reused for more than one day of microinjection.

steps.title: Prepare fecal‑charcoal plates (uninfected)
steps.instruction: On the day of microinjection, collect fresh feces from uninfected Mongolian gerbils in an ABSL‑2 vivarium. Mix the feces with an equal volume of autoclaved charcoal and enough water to make a uniform slurry. Spread the mixture onto a 6‑cm Petri dish to form a fecal‑charcoal plate.

steps.title: Microinject free‑living females
steps.instruction: Using the prepared agarose pads, intragonadally microinject free‑living adult females with either Microinjection Mix 1 or Mix 2 as appropriate. After injection, transfer the injected females together with non‑injected free‑living males onto the freshly prepared fecal‑charcoal plates.

steps.title: Collect F3 iL3s from gerbil
steps.instruction: After at least 14 days post‑oral‑gavage (optimal around day 23), collect host feces and prepare fecal‑charcoal plates as in step 5. Incubate plates at 23 °C for 7–10 days to allow post‑parasitic young larvae to develop into iL3s.

substeps.instruction: Collect iL3s with a Baermann apparatus; wait 2–3 h before harvesting to maximize yield.
Store harvested iL3s in BU saline in a microcentrifuge tube (or begin screening after 1 h if preferred).

steps.title: Screen for dual‑fluorescent iL3s
steps.instruction: Transfer iL3s in 2–10 µL droplets onto an E. coli OP50 agar plate and let the droplets dry so worms disperse. Under a fluorescence dissecting microscope, identify iL3s that co‑express GFP and mScarlet‑I in body‑wall muscle. Pick each dual‑colored iL3 with a paintbrush into watch glasses containing ~1 mL BU saline, keeping ≤75–100 iL3s per glass. Aim to collect ~200 dual‑colored iL3s (2–3 watch glasses).

substeps.instruction: Avoid picking non‑fluorescent or single‑color iL3s by keeping worm density low on the plate.
If fewer than ~200 dual‑colored iL3s are obtained, repeat Baermann collection and screening.

steps.title: Activate screened iL3s
steps.instruction: Incubate the pooled dual‑colored iL3s for 36–42 h under activation conditions as described elsewhere (e.g., exposure to host‑mimicking cues).

steps.title: Infect gerbils with activated iL3s
steps.instruction: Orally gavage one or more gerbils with the activated iL3s (≈200 iL3s is sufficient; up to 500 can be used for robust infection; up to 800 may be tried if initial infection fails). Include a backup gerbil that receives the wash from the gavage needle. Keep backup gerbils housed separately.

steps.title: Maintain and propagate stable line
steps.instruction: Once the line is established, infect two or more gerbils with ~500 activated iL3s each and co‑house (≤5 gerbils per cage). Collect feces together, prepare fecal‑charcoal plates, and repeat steps 8–12 for successive generations. Visual confirmation that the entire iL3 population expresses at least one fluorophore is required before each passage; if non‑fluorescent iL3s appear, repeat the red/green selection.

steps.title: Optional: Propagate with non‑activated iL3s
steps.instruction: Wash iL3s three times in sterile 1× PBS, resuspend in sterile 1× PBS, and orally gavage into gerbils. Do not use non‑activated iL3s that were previously screened on OP50 plates. Establish a parallel mixed‑population line as a backup (see step 13).

steps.title: Establish mixed‑population backup line
steps.instruction: Collect GFP‑only and mScarlet‑only iL3s (from F2/F3 generations) and pool them. Infect a host with this mixed population to maintain both fluorophore‑expressing lines. Before each host passage, verify that both GFP‑positive and mScarlet‑positive iL3s are present; actively select each phenotype every 2–3 generations to preserve both alleles.
